### JBMC's phases are exclusive: post-processing counted once, overcounts flagged (verification pending)

change `snprkxtxpqkt` · [log `fa4801646280`](https://terminalvalue.net/raw-traces/7b8a1d3b-6fbf-40ab-b647-1f9fc12bc573/fa480164628072b09bc0f215aa3dbfec879e0e194e60e2baea7ea375b67f66a9.jsonl.gz)

Phase 1a of engine-priorities.md, in the jbmc stream. CBMC 6.11.0's 'Runtime Solver' times a whole solver call, including the 'Runtime Post-process' reported from inside it. lib/src/phases.rs counted both, so JBMC's phases added up past the run, for example 22.0 s of phases in 15.9 s on held/reverse in job 20261106-102624. It now reads the timers per solver call. Post-processing counts as encoding, and the rest of the call as solving. A call that never reached the SAT solver (out of memory while post-processing) counts entirely as encoding. A run cut off mid-call still gives the rest of its time to the phase it was in.

Phases::excess flags a run whose named phases add up past its seconds by more than 1% plus 5 ms. The excess is recorded as phases_excess on each checker run, never scaled to fit. lib/benchmark/run.py carries it as phasesExcess and leaves such runs out of the 'Where the time goes' tables, naming them below. The recorded RESULTS.md (job -102624) stands as written, and its README now says its JBMC shares overcount.

Verified against real JBMC 6.11.0 output captured on cvm, kept as fixtures in lib/tests/fixtures/jbmc-phases/ (README says how each was made): held/prefix-sums proved, the same cut off by a 1.9 s budget, held/reverse out of memory at 700 MiB, and a run with two solver calls. The tests check each phase against JBMC's own Runtime figures, that the phases add up to the run, and that the old double count is flagged. The Rust lib (150), integration (63) and skill tests pass, as do lib/benchmark/test_run.py's 19. conformance.rs's the_corpus_agrees_with_the_jvm_on_the_tools_own_checker fails on cvm with 12 disagreements. Its messages point to the contract library's records being for JDK 25.0.4.1 while cvm has 25.0.5, not to this change; this is recorded under Progress for the reconcile loop.

Job 20261106-192959 fetches CBMC's source at the cbmc-6.11.0 tag (a network fetch, inside the job) and checks that the timers nest as the fixtures show.

### JBMC's staging policy is an option: staged, full range alone, or one tight stage first

change `uykqwxvrwywl` · [log `0d78378a22c8`](https://terminalvalue.net/raw-traces/7b8a1d3b-6fbf-40ab-b647-1f9fc12bc573/0d78378a22c84361d50834a255abd83c43adedf45f5e86b4a97c59c4130e94fd.jsonl.gz)

Step 2a of llm-dlc/loops/engine-priorities.md. `--jbmc-staging` on `equivalence` and `prove` picks which of JBMC's interval stages run before the full range (`deadline::Staging`). `staged` is today's search and stays the default until the 2b job decides. `full-range` runs the full range alone and shrinks its counterexample in the interpreter. `tight` runs the first stage that leaves out an input on at most a fortieth of the check, then the full range. The deadline, bounds, models, preflights, gap rules and stop rule are the same under each, and the own checker's stages and --confirm don't follow the policy. A JBMC verdict records the policy as search.staging.

Verified with unit tests in deadline.rs for each policy's stages and budgets, and an end-to-end test in conformance.rs (added) against a stand-in JBMC answering stage by stage. It checks the stages and budgets on property and regression checks, a slow first stage handing on, and violations from the wide stage and the full range, both shrunk to the same witness. Mutating equivalence to ignore the option fails it. Lib 155, integration 63 and skill tests pass. Conformance fails only as before: 12 JDK 25.0.5 disagreements in the corpus test, recorded in Progress. Shared files are named under Progress. Noted for 2c: under --engine auto, a staged fallback whose two preliminary stages time out leaves the full range no time.

### JBMC lets a runtime exception past its handler in two shapes: the preflight names them and refuses a JBMC proof through one (verification pending)

change `svvrpymrpslx` · [log `51b81ecca682`](https://terminalvalue.net/raw-traces/7b8a1d3b-6fbf-40ab-b647-1f9fc12bc573/51b81ecca682bda21cc8c857d8ccf3d0fb69076f0b95e14c7eaa0f0cec4d4377.jsonl.gz)

Step 3 of llm-dlc/loops/engine-priorities.md. JBMC's counterexamples to conformance/caught/1 and nestedHandler/1 (n=0) did not reproduce because JBMC 6.11.0 lets a runtime exception past the handler that catches it on the JVM, so the exception escapes the method. It is not the models, the harness, or the trace reading. There are two shapes, found by running JBMC (milliseconds) on the cases and on variants of them, written up in lib/tests/fixtures/jbmc-defects/README.md. (1) A JBMC defect: for 'try { return 10 / n; } catch (ArithmeticException e)', javac ends the handler's range before ireturn, and JBMC emits the quotient, with the check --throw-runtime-exceptions adds, at the ireturn, after its pop_catch. The same holds for irem, ldiv, lrem, array elements, fields and arraylength. (2) This repository's class path: JBMC's stub of a JDK exception class has no superclass, so 'catch (RuntimeException e)' misses an ArithmeticException or IllegalArgumentException. Both shapes also gave false proofs under strict with --engine jbmc: caught, with --throws 'java.lang.ArithmeticException when n == 0', was proved, while the JVM returns -1.

JBMC's preflight (lib/src/jbmc_gaps.rs) now finds both shapes in the bytecode JBMC reaches, as return-past-handler and stubbed-handler defects. A JBMC proof that reaches one is no verdict under every gap mode. A counterexample is still replayed, and prove's message names the defect when it doesn't reproduce. Tests: a unit test over 8 shapes in tests/fixtures/jbmc-defects/p/D.java (4 defects, 4 neighbours JBMC runs as the JVM does), which fails with the detection disabled, and one for hold. End to end on the real JBMC, both false proofs are now refused (under assume too), caught/1 and nestedHandler/1 are unverifiable naming the defect, and exactCatch is still a violation. The corpus gains caught/3 and caughtAsRuntime/1 and /2 (lib/benchmark/conformance.json regenerated); they agree with the JVM on the own checker, and the inline test fails only on its 12 known JDK 25.0.5 disagreements. The lib unit tests (157), the other conformance tests and test_run.py pass. A report for cause 1 is drafted in the fixture's README for the user, not filed. The fix for cause 2, models of the exception hierarchy, belongs in lib/models and is recorded for the reconcile loop.

Job 20261106-203452 runs what needs JBMC: the integration tests, and the ignored conformance tests under jbmc, auto and auto --confirm.

Shared files changed, added to: lib/src/property.rs (the replay message asks the preflight first), lib/tests/conformance.rs and Conformance.java (three claims, one method), lib/README.md (a paragraph).

**Reply:**

The step 3 commit stands (`svvrpymrpslx`), with job `20261106-203452` pending. JBMC's two witnesses that didn't reproduce turned out to hide false proofs. JBMC can now no longer give those proofs: they come back with no verdict.

**Why the witnesses didn't reproduce.** JBMC 6.11.0 lets a runtime exception get past a handler that catches it on the JVM, so the exception escapes the method. It isn't the models or how the trace is read. There are two shapes:
- **A JBMC bug (`return-past-handler`).** In `try { return 10 / n; } catch (ArithmeticException e)`, javac ends the handler's range just before the `return`. JBMC computes `10 / n`, and the division-by-zero check that throws, at the `return`, after the handler has already closed. The same happens for remainders, `long` division, array elements, fields and array lengths. Storing the value in a local first, passing it to a call, comparing it, or using `finally` is unaffected. `caught/1` is this shape.
- **This repo's class path (`stubbed-handler`).** JBMC has no class files for the JDK's exception classes, and its stand-ins for them have no superclass. So `catch (RuntimeException e)` misses an `ArithmeticException` or `IllegalArgumentException`. `nestedHandler/1` has both shapes.
